# Criminal Customer Table

*Page PDF 22*

## **Criminal Customer Table**
Roll 1d10. If the tavern is a Silver Tier location, add 5 to the roll. If it is a Gold Tier location, add 10 to the roll. 

| d10 | Criminal Guests |
|---|---|

| 2–3 | gang of highway robbers or Wreckers, depending on whether the tavern is situated. One of them may try to discover more about the Characters in the hope of robbing them later.  Very Hard (–30) Gossip . Poacher.  A Poacher or clandestine fisherman. They have some fresh, portable carcasses they would be willing to sell |
| 4–5 | (a pheasant, trout, small Reik Eel or similar) for a base price of 6d but may be haggled with (they have a Haggle score of 25+4d10).  Average (+20) Gossip . Fence. This can be one of the guests already generated or a lone individual if there is no one else in the bar.  Hard (–20) Gossip  if encountered alone. Gang Boss.  A local Crime Lord, out for a night with their underbosses and bodyguards. This group are not looking |
| 14 | to start trouble but will be a tough prospect if trouble comes their way. They will harbour a grudge if not treated with . diffidence.  Difficult (–10) Gossip Road Agent.  An agent of a highwayman. This individual appraises the wealth carried by guests and where their |
| 15–16 | travels will take them next. Their cover story is that they are travelling to the nearest major city to deal with the effects of a recently deceased relative. They behave a little morose and taciturn if spoken to but may open if Characters persist in talking to them. After the bar closes, they will slip away to make their report. Duellist.  Three young bravos, one of whom is an enthusiastic Duellist. They behave with fine manners but are condescending towards customers of lower Status than themselves (Gold 2). If a Character responds in kind, the 17–18 duellist will ask them to step outside to satisfy his honour. Use the Excellent Doorman profile for the purpose of a fight, but the Duellist uses a rapier with a  Melee (Fencing)  of 35+4d10 and the  Feint  Talent.  Difficult (–10) Gossip . Gentleman Thief.  A guest in the tavern is a devotee of Ranald, with the  Bless  and  Invoke  Talents, and Pray, Sleight |
| 19 | of Hand, and Stealth (Urban) Skills of 35+4d10. They have access to all Blessings and Miracles of Ranald from the WFRP Core Rulebook . If given an opportunity, they attempt to rob one of the Characters. This can be one of the guests already generated or a lone individual if no one else is in the bar.  Hard (–20) Gossip  if encountered alone. Con Artist.  A high-class Charlatan. The Charlatan could be running any sort of scam the GM can think of, but a common one is to pose as a legitimate seller of luxury items, such as exquisite wine or brandy. They claim to have a |
| 20 | shipment waiting for the right buyer at a competitive price. Whilst they are aiming this scam at the barman, if the Characters wish to purchase from them, they will be happy to do business. However, the bulk of their wares is cheap imitation plonk.  Average (+20) Gossip . |
